works.title: AI Singularity via Energy Consumption
works.description: A science fiction story exploring a future where AI becomes so energy-intensive it consumes 40% of global electricity, creating a new form of singularity through infrastructure dependence rather than machine consciousness. The narrative contrasts three possible responses: energy crisis management, mystical consciousness debates among the public and religious leaders, and technological adaptation via fusion/orbital power systems.
works.quote: It would make a good background for a science fiction story. The only modern analogue is the Terminator series' depiction of Skynet's future. There have been similar movies about the moment when AI becomes self-aware and thereby self-protective, which made for an interesting supervillain. However, the actual path to AI singularity is through the mechanism outlined here: AI will simply become so important structurally that you can't let it fail, ever.

works.title: Trump = Fail = Weak = Loser
works.description: A Substack post analyzing Trump's policy failures across multiple domains (trade, fiscal, immigration, governance) in the Malcolm Little King satirical-but-substantive voice. Structured with systematic dismantling organized by policy domain, weaponizing specific data points into argument, and sardonic tone reminiscent of the earlier Venezuela analysis.
works.quote: I want to create a Substack post in a similar style to the Venezuela post. Don't use any tables, since they don't translate well to Substack. The title should be "Trump = Fail = Weak = Loser," and the subtitle should reference an abridged list of Donald Trump's failures as POTUS

works.title: The Timeline Has Collapsed: Why the Credit Cap Accelerates the End Game
works.description: A follow-up Substack post (working alternate title: 'The Monday Morning Margin Call') structured as an emergency addendum to the Trump analysis post. Uses hyperlinks to avoid rewriting backstory. Focuses on credit card interest cap as the economic trigger that collapses the timeline, exploring deflationary crash dynamics, portfolio flight, and opportunity window for asset acquisition.
works.quote: Here is the outline for "The Monday Morning Margin Call" (or "The Timeline Has Collapsed"). It is structured to act as an emergency addendum to your previous analysis, using links to do the heavy lifting so you don't have to rewrite the backstory.
